What do you like best about Asana?

I use Asana for daily project management and really like its intuitive interface with powerful workflow automation. The ability to switch seamlessly between List, Board, and Timeline views gives me clear visibility into project progress. I also appreciate features like custom intake forms, automated task assignment rules, and AI-powered reporting that cut down on manual work. Plus, the integrations with Slack, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Teams keep our team connected and aligned in one central hub. The initial setup was easy and straightforward, and Asana's user-friendly design and pre-built project templates made onboarding quick. We were able to start working in minutes, without complex technical configuration. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

While Asana is great for general project management, managing very complex projects with extensive task dependencies can sometimes become visually cluttered and hard to navigate. Additionally, the pricing model can be restrictive for scaling teams. It would be a huge improvement if Asana offered more flexible, tiered seat options—such as lower-cost 'view-only' seats—so external stakeholders or casual team members can track progress without requiring full-price licenses. "Intuitive UI, Strong Collaboration, and Handy Slack Integration"
4/5
What do you like best about Asana?

I like the UI/UX aspects of collaboration, custom template, and dependencies features. They help the team stay on the same project and give everyone visibility into the status (or lack thereof) of specific tasks or an overall vertical that we’re working on. Also integration with Slack is helpful because we can pull tasks directly from chats within our DMs or channels. With templates, we can also build in common elements across projects that share the same known tasks, so we don’t miss repeatable steps on specific projects. Being able to analyze common points between tasks ahead of time would make it easier to streamline how we create those templates. And if we already had pre-built dependencies, we could use them as a starting point for suggesting due dates, whether we’re planning forward or working backward from a set deadline. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

I think what is unfortunate, is the lack of ability to custom assign roles. To have all the members we want to have on Asana it's much higher overhead than what's worth spending at this time, however, if there were tiered roles that we could assign and one person (for instance) would have a basic "view" seat at $5/mo but another who's Admin was at a higher $30/mo, with a middle ground of "regular user" being at $15/mo that would allow more of the team to be on the platform, without necessarily having the ability (or need) to utilize the platform to it's full capacity, while also having the company analyze the performance of who actually needs an Admin seat. Also, interchanging those roles would be helpful for onboarding purposes; for instance if a new member joins, and we want to have visibility into a project without them actually being able to mark something as complete - but rather just a backseat watcher, they could have a view only seat so they could track how the status of a task or project goes along the way and when the team is ready they could be moved into a different tier role at a higher price paid seat. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

Honestly, prior to utilizing Asana, there was no way of tracking tasks and projects. The KPIs were essentially non visible in the sense of being able to track/prove performance of a team member or overall department. Being able to utilize project tracking status allows us to see how far along each vertical is OR how long a project has to be complete. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.
